cards.explanation: The answer is all people, because all sinned. Paul says it plainly: “…death was passed on to all men, because all sinned.” (Romans 5:12) Adam, the first man (1 Corinthians 15:45), is where it started, but he isn't the only name on the list. Hold onto your hats, friends, because the good news is coming.

The answer is Moses. Paul says death reigned from Adam until Moses. Moses, Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), is the one the law came through (John 1:17). So Paul's point is that death was already reigning before the law was given (Romans 5:13-14). Nobody had to write it up for death to show up.

The answer is False. Here's what Paul says: death reigned “…even over those who did not sin in the way that Adam transgressed.” (Romans 5:14) Death didn't keep a guest list. It reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who did not sin in the way Adam transgressed.

The answer is Jesus Christ. Paul names Him right in the next verse: “…the one man, Jesus Christ…” (Romans 5:15) Adam is a pattern, and Jesus is who the pattern points to. One man's act reached the many, and so does the other's. I stamp patterns for a living, and even I didn't see that one coming.

The answer is False. Paul says it flat out: “But the gift is not like the trespass.” (Romans 5:15) They sit side by side, but they aren't equals. Then he says how much more God's grace and the gift abound to the many.

The answer is God's grace through Jesus Christ. Paul's words are “…how much more did God’s grace and the gift that came by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many!” (Romans 5:15) The trespass was real, but grace goes further. That makes me want to wave my mustache.

The answer is being made right with God. Paul's word is justification: “…the gift that followed many trespasses brought justification.” (Romans 5:16) It's the opposite of condemnation. Think about that: the gift followed many trespasses, not just one. Now that's a gift worth unwrapping, friends.

The answer is True. Paul says it just that way: “…those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one man, Jesus Christ!” (Romans 5:17) Death reigned through one man, and those who receive will reign in life through another. Notice the word receive, friends. It's a gift, so the job is to take it.

The answer is righteousness. Paul says “…so also one act of righteousness brought justification and life for all men.” (Romans 5:18) One trespass on one side, one act of righteousness on the other. It's a clean match, and it ends with life.

The answers are disobedience and obedience. Paul says the many were made sinners “…through the disobedience of the one man…” (Romans 5:19). One man's disobedience, and it reached the many. It's a heavy word, but it sets up the turn that's coming. Paul says the many will be made righteous “…through the obedience of the one man…” (Romans 5:19). Disobedience on one side, obedience on the other. That's the swap, and it's the best one in the whole passage.
The answer is False. Paul says “The law came in so that the trespass would increase…” (Romans 5:20) Increase, not shrink. It sounds backwards at first, but he's not done with the sentence yet.

The answer is that grace increased all the more. Paul says “…where sin increased, grace increased all the more…” (Romans 5:20) However high sin got, grace went higher. If I could stamp that on a cookie, I'd need a stamper the size of the Dorinverse.

The answers are sin and grace. Paul says “…just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness to bring eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” (Romans 5:21) Sin reigned in death, and that's the low note he sets up so the next one can ring out. Sin had its reign, and now grace gets one. This one ends in eternal life, friends. I'm doing a little hop on my gold base.
